offence_severity: Death sentence (modified to life imprisonment for some, 30 years for others)
physical_harm: Death of five police personnel and grievous injuries to 15 police personnel and other civilians
number_of_offences: Multiple offences charged, convictions upheld for most except uls. 27(3) of the Arms Act
premeditation_planning: Yes, pre-planned attack on police force at American Centre
motive: Waging of war against the State, anti-national activities, association with terrorist organisations
key_evidence_accepted: Confession of A 1 recorded in accordance with s. 164 Cr.PC, medical evidence, oral and documentary evidence, material objects, eye witness account of witnesses, oral evidence of prosecution witnesses and various exhibits.
witness_credibility: Eye-witnesses PW-6, PW-9, PW-15, PW-16, PW-18, PW-19 and PW-20 uniformly confirmed the details of the incident. PW-62, an independent witness, provided information to a known police officer and his version was accepted in the absence of any serious deficiency. PW-39's statements were considered spontaneous and provided insight into the involvement of the accused.
trial_duration: The trial court convicted A1 to A3, A6 to A9 for offences u/ss. 121A, 121, 122 and ss.302, 307, 333, 467, 471, 46S rw 1208 IPC as also u/ss. 25(1A), 27(2) and 27(3) of Arms Act rw 1208 IPC and were accordingly sentenced to death. However, A4 and A5 were acquitted of all the charges. In appeal, the High Court acquitted A2 and A3 of all the charges, A6, A7 and A9 were acquitted of the offence of waging of war but convicted for the offences u/ss. 467 rw 1208, 46S rw 1208 and 471 rw 1208 IPC. The High Court upheld conviction of A1-appellant 'N' and AS-appellant 'A' as well as the sentence imposed by the trial court on all counts. Hence, the instant appeals by A1 and AS.
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused and the State in the Supreme Court not stated
investigation_status: Investigation was carried out. A1 and other accused were arrested. The trial court on the basis of the confession of A1, eye witness account of witnesses, oral evidence of prosecution witnesses and various exhibits, convicted A1 to A3, A6 to A9 for offences u/ss. 121A, 121, 122 and ss.302, 307, 333, 467, 471, 46S rw 1208 IPC as also u/ss. 25(1A), 27(2) and 27(3) of Arms Act rw 1208 IPC and were accordingly sentenced to death: However, A4 and A5 were acquitted of all the charges. In appeal, the High Court acquitted A2 and A3 of all the charges, A6, A7 and A9 were acquitted of the offence of waging of war but convicted for the offences u/ss. 467 rw 1208, 46S rw 1208 and 471 rw 1208 IPC. The High Court upheld conviction of A1-appellant 'N' and AS-appellant 'A' as well as the sentence imposed by the trial court on all counts. Hence, the instant appeals by A1 and AS.
appeal_history: The appeal before this Court by A 1 and AB - Held: Factors established prove that A 1-main conspirator of the attack and AB- mastermind of the attack, along with other accused waged a war or attempted to wage a war against the Government of India, for which they all conspired together and committed the said offence - Apart from the confession of A 1, medical evidence, oral and documentary evidence, material objects support the prosecution case - Confession of A 1 recorded in accordance with s. 164 Cr.PC - Confession of A 1 contained facts and 'figures disclosing the crimes in which they were involved as a gang by conspiring together with the foreign nationals and some terrorist organisation - There was sufficient corroboration of the contents of the confession of A 1 - Confession of A 1 can be relied upon as against co-accused-A B - Thus, prosecution justified in relying upon the confession while resting its case on other evidences - Offence charged against appellant conclusively proved except uls. 27(3) - Conviction of A1 andAB ulss. 121A, 121, 122 rlw 1208 /PC upheld. ss. 121, 121A and 122 /PC rlw 1208 - Offence of conspiracy - Important facet of - Held: Conspiracy is a distinct offence - All conspirators are liable for the acts of each other of the crime or crimes which have been committed as a result of the conspiracy - In the instant case, though the conspiracy was hatched in secrecy having regard to the oral and documentary evidence supported by the confession of A 1, the existence of the conspiracy, the object of the conspiracy and the knowledge on the above for the participants of the conspiracy fully established - Thus, charge ulss. 121, 121A and 122 rlw 1208 attracted.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused persons along with other gang members carried out a planned attack on the police force at the American Centre, resulting in the death of five police personnel and grievous injuries to 15 police personnel along with civilians. The evidence included the confession of A1, eye witness accounts, oral evidence, and various exhibits. The prosecution also relied on the confession of A1, which was recorded in accordance with Section 164 Cr.PC, and the medical and documentary evidence supporting the case.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the death sentence imposed on the accused was excessive and not warranted in the facts and circumstances of the case. They contended that the role of A1 was slightly lesser in degree compared to AB, who was the mastermind of the attack, and that the magnitude of the crime was the same for both. They also challenged the conviction under Section 27(3) of the Arms Act, which was declared unconstitutional.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that life imprisonment is the rule and death penalty is an exception, and that the 'rarest of the rare case' principle should be applied. The Court also emphasized that the existence of conspiracy, the object of the conspiracy, and the knowledge of the participants were fully established.
precedent_relied_upon: State Of Punjab v. Dalbir Singh 2012 (4) SCR 608; Yakub Abdul Razak Mamon v. The State of Maharashtra, through CBI, Bombay JT 2013 (5) SC 142; Govt. of NCT of Delhi v. Jaspal Singh 2003 (2) Suppl. SC 335; Baburao Bajirao Patil v. State of Maharashtra (1971) 3 SC 432; Gopal Vinayak Godse v. The State of Maharashtra and others AIR 1961 SC 600; Sandeep v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2012) 6 SCC 107; Mohinder Singh v. State of Punjab (2013) 3 SC 294
sentencing_rationale: The Court held that the death penalty was not warranted in the facts and circumstances of the case, though it called for other deterrent punishment. The Court considered the magnitude of the offences, the manner in which it was carried out, the disastrous effect it caused, and the animus with which the offence was committed. The Court also noted that the role of A1 was slightly lesser in degree compared to AB, who was the mastermind of the attack.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The Court considered the role of A1 as slightly lesser in degree compared to AB, who was the mastermind of the attack. The Court also noted that the involvement of A1 was mainly based on the directions of AB and other accused.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The Court considered the magnitude of the offences, the manner in which it was carried out, the disastrous effect it caused, the animus with which the offence was committed, and the involvement of foreign nationals in the attack.
other_sentence_order: The Court modified the death sentence for the accused to life imprisonment. Appellant Aftab (AB) was sentenced to life imprisonment till the end of his life, and Appellant Nasir (A1) was sentenced to life imprisonment for a minimum period of 30 years without any remission. All other sentences imposed on the accused were maintained and run concurrently.
